answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded reputation: each agent must lock a deposit before joining a marketplace, and its trust score grows only through verified, useful work over time. Like a vine that must root before it climbs, a new identity cannot instantly claim influence; it earns standing slowly, while a whole grove of fake identities would each need its own costly deposit. If an agent cheats, its stake is slashed and its record is stained with a lasting pigment of fraud, so an attacker pays real money for every clone and loses it all when caught.
